mainTopic: When the כהן משיח's sin counts as separate, and what is needed for the court and the כהן משיח to be liable, including for עבודה זרה
overview: The amud opens with רב פפא explaining that the case involves a כהן משיח and judges who were both qualified to rule. אביי and רבא then define when the כהן משיח 'sinned by himself': רבא says ruling on a different prohibition is enough, even in the same room. The גמרא asks whether two kinds of חלב from different verses count as two prohibitions. Assuming they do not, it asks the same about חלב and blood, which bring the same קרבן but have different sources, and that question ends in תיקו. Next the גמרא finds the sources for the משנה's rules: the court and the כהן משיח are liable only for a partial ruling, even for עבודה זרה. A new משנה then teaches that liability needs both a mistaken ruling and an action done because of it, with the sources brought for each case. Finally, the גמרא discusses a כהן משיח who sins with עבודה זרה. It suggests the משנה follows רבי, rejects that proof, and explains how רבי and the רבנן read the same פסוק differently. It ends by showing that everyone agrees he brings a female goat like any individual.

steps.title: רב פפא: both were qualified to rule
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the case is one where both the כהן משיח and the judges were מופלין, meaning qualified to issue rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: the case is where both of them were distinguished scholars.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains which case the משנה is talking about. Both the כהן משיח and the judges were qualified scholars who could issue rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mistaken ruling only counts as a real הוראה if it comes from someone qualified to rule. So רב פפא makes clear that the כהן משיח's ruling, and the judges' ruling, both carry legal weight.

keyTerms.meaning: Distinguished scholars, fully qualified to issue rulings
The anointed כהן גדול
For example; this is the kind of case

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For example, where both of them were distinguished scholars.
phrases.notes: 'Both of them' means the כהן משיח and the judges of the בית דין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיוּ מוּפְלִין שְׁנֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question about the משנה's case that came just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is one where both the כהן משיח and the judges were qualified to rule.

steps.title: אביי's first idea: two places, two prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: אביי assumes that 'sinned by himself' means the כהן משיח and the בית דין sat in different places and ruled on different prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי thought: what is the case of 'sinned by himself and acted by himself'? It is where they sat in two places and ruled on two different prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a first guess at what the משנה means by the כהן משיח sinning 'by himself.' This sets up רבא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'סבר למימר' tell us this is only an initial thought that will be corrected. אביי's picture needs two things to make the sin separate: different locations and different prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say; an initial idea that will be corrected
He sinned by himself, separately from the community
What is the case? How do we picture it?
They issue rulings

phrases.english: Abaye thought to say:

phrases.aramaic: חָטָא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְעָשָׂה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: 'He sinned by himself and acted by himself'
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words about the כהן משיח.

phrases.english: what is the case?
Where they were sitting in two places
and were ruling about two different prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to defining the משנה's other case, where the כהן משיח sins on his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First idea: a separate sin needs both separate places and separate prohibitions.

steps.title: רבא: does location really matter?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי, asking whether sitting in two places is really what makes the sin separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: do two places make the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's idea. He asks why the physical location should matter at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אטו' marks a rhetorical challenge. Where people sit is not a legal factor. What makes a sin separate must be the content of the ruling, not the room it was given in.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? A rhetorical challenge
Cause, determine

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Is that to say that two places are what determine it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אַטּוּ שְׁנֵי מְקוֹמוֹת גּוֹרְמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks one part of אביי's definition, the 'two places' requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's requirement that they sit in two different places
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Physical location has no legal meaning here. Only the subject of the ruling should matter.

steps.title: רבא: two different prohibitions are enough
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that even in one place, if they ruled on two different prohibitions, the כהן משיח has sinned by himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, even if they sat in one place, since they ruled about two prohibitions, he sinned by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the correct definition. Different prohibitions alone make the כהן משיח's sin separate, wherever they were sitting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא drops the 'two places' condition and keeps only 'two prohibitions.' This sets up the rest of the section, which asks what counts as 'two different prohibitions.'

keyTerms.meaning: In one place
Two different prohibitions

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the test for 'sinned by himself' is whether the כהן משיח ruled on a different prohibition than the בית דין. Location does not matter.
steps.whyThisMatters: Everything that follows in this section tries to define when two rulings count as 'two prohibitions.'

phrases.english: Rather, even if they were sitting in one place,
since they are ruling about two different prohibitions,
it is a case of 'he sinned by himself.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's definition with a simpler one, following from the challenge.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Two different prohibitions alone make the כהן משיח's sin separate, even in one place.

steps.title: Obvious case: priest on fat, court on idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that if the כהן משיח ruled about חלב and the court ruled about עבודה זרה, his sin is separate. Their sources differ, and their קרבנות differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if he ruled on forbidden fat and they ruled on idol worship, he sinned by himself. The rulings differ in their reasons, and they differ in their offerings: he brings a bull, they bring a bull and a goat, so they bring a goat and he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists a clear case that obviously counts as two prohibitions. This begins a build-up toward the harder question at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate differences appear here. First, the reasons differ: each prohibition comes from its own source. Second, the קרבנות differ: the court adds a שעיר for עבודה זרה, which the כהן משיח does not bring.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
Forbidden fat of an animal
They differ in their reasons, meaning their sources in the תורה
A bull
A male goat

phrases.aramaic: פְּשִׁיטָא: הוּא בְּחֵלֶב וְהֵן בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה –
phrases.english: It is obvious: if he ruled on forbidden fat and they ruled on idol worship,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן משיח and 'they' are the judges of the בית דין.

phrases.english: it is a case of 'he sinned by himself,'
since they differ in their reasons
and they differ in their offerings.
For he brings a bull, and they bring a bull and a goat.
So these bring a goat,
and he does not bring one.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא: הוּא בְּחֵלֶב וְהֵן בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's 'two prohibitions' test to an easy case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fat and עבודה זרה are clearly separate sins: different sources and different קרבנות.

steps.title: Even more obvious: priest on idol worship, court on fat
steps.stepSummary: The reverse case is even clearer, because there the קרבנות are completely different: a female goat for him and a bull for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the more so if he ruled on idol worship and they ruled on fat, since their offerings are totally different: he brings a female goat, and they bring a bull.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a קל וחומר: the reverse case is even more clearly a separate sin. This continues the build-up toward the real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the two sides at least shared a bull. Here the offerings share nothing: a שעירה for the כהן משיח and a פר for the court. So the difference is even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so
Completely
A female goat

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן הוּא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהֵן בְּחֵלֶב,
phrases.english: And all the more so if he ruled on idol worship and they ruled on forbidden fat,
since they differ [completely] in their offerings:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in square brackets and some don't.

phrases.english: for he brings a female goat, and they bring a bull.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן הוּא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהֵן בְּחֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a קל וחומר on step 5's obvious case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reverse case is a separate sin even more clearly, since the offerings are entirely different.

steps.title: The real question: two kinds of forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the כהן משיח ruled about the fat covering the innards and the court ruled about the fat on the small intestines. Are these two prohibitions because they come from two verses, or one, since it is all 'חלב'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what if he ruled on the fat covering the innards and they ruled on the fat on the small intestines? Do we say that even though their offerings are the same, they come from two verses and so differ in their reasons? Or perhaps it is all one category of fat?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks its real question. Both rulings are about forbidden fat, so the קרבנות are the same. Does the fact that each kind of fat comes from a different verse make them two prohibitions?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5 and 6 had two differences: reasons and offerings. Here only one possible difference is left, the separate verses, since the offerings match. The question is whether separate verses alone count as 'different reasons,' or whether all חלב is one name and one prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The fat that covers the innards
The fat on the small intestines
What is the law?
Verses
Or perhaps
One name, one category

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the question is about the offerings. Both sides agree the קרבנות here are identical. The only question is whether separate verses make 'different reasons.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sharpens רבא's test: does 'two prohibitions' mean two separate sources in the פסוקים, or two separate categories of sin?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הוּא בְּחֵלֶב הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת הַקֶּרֶב,
phrases.english: Rather, if he ruled on the fat that covers the innards,
and they ruled on the fat that is on the small intestines, what is the law?
Do we say:
Even though their offering is the same,
since they come from two different verses,
they differ in their reasons?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא שֵׁם חֵלֶב אֶחָד הוּא?
phrases.english: Or perhaps 'forbidden fat' is one single category?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הוּא בְּחֵלֶב הַמְכַסֶּה אֶת הַקֶּרֶב, וְהֵן בְּחֵלֶב שֶׁעַל הַדַּקִּין, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the obvious cases, the גמרא moves to the hard case where only one of the two differences might apply.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether two kinds of חלב from separate verses, with the same קרבן, count as two prohibitions, so that the כהן משיח 'sinned by himself.'

steps.title: The priest rules about fat, the court rules about blood
steps.stepSummary: Suppose all חלב is one prohibition. If the כהן משיח rules about חלב and the court rules about blood, are these separate sins because their sources differ? Or are they one, since they bring the same kind of קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say all fat is one prohibition, what if he ruled about fat and they ruled about blood? Do we say they differ because each has its own source? Or, since they bring the same offering, do we go by the offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on the question in step 7 and asks a new one. This time the two rulings are about חלב and blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5 the sins were separate for two reasons: different sources and different קרבנות. Here only one reason is present. חלב and blood come from different פסוקים, but they bring the same קרבן. The question is which factor decides.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (assuming one side of the previous question)
Blood, which is forbidden to eat
In their reasons, meaning their separate sources in the תורה
We follow the offering

phrases.english: If you say
phrases.notes: This takes the second side of the question in step 7 and builds on it.

phrases.english: that the name 'fat' is one,
if he ruled about fat and they ruled about blood,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן משיח and 'they' are the court.

phrases.english: what is the law?
Do we say:
in their reasons they are different,
or perhaps
since they are the same in their offering
we go by the offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the question in step 7 by assuming one side of it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When only the source differs and the קרבן is the same, are the two rulings separate?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The question about חלב and blood is left open: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not find an answer, so it leaves the question open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side wins. We do not know whether different sources or the same קרבן decides.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: If the priest and the court ruled about prohibitions that bring the same קרבן but have different sources, whether his sin is separate stays undecided.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes step 8 without an answer.

steps.title: Source for needing a partial ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the court is liable only if they ruled to cancel part of a מצוה and keep part. It then asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the court is not liable unless they rule to cancel part and keep part. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks for the source of one of its rules. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that if the court uproots a whole מצוה, they do not bring a קרבן. They are liable only when they cancel a detail and keep the rest. The גמרא wants a פסוק for this.

keyTerms.meaning: The court
To cancel part and keep part
From where do we know?

phrases.english: That the court is not liable
unless they rule to cancel part
and to keep part, etc.
From where do we know
that it is only when they rule to cancel part
and keep part?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that explains the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for requiring a partial ruling.

steps.title: The source is the word 'דבר'
steps.stepSummary: As learned earlier in the מסכת, 'ונעלם דבר' means only a 'thing' was hidden, not the whole מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we said in the other chapter: 'And a thing is hidden': a thing, and not the whole body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to a דרשה it already taught earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'a thing' was hidden from the court. That suggests one detail was missed. If the whole מצוה was forgotten, that is not 'a thing', so there is no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The other chapter (earlier in this מסכת)
And a thing was hidden (from the פסוק)
The whole body of the מצוה

phrases.english: As we said in the other chapter:
phrases.notes: He means earlier in this מסכת, on daf 3b.

phrases.english: "And a thing is hidden"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: "a thing", and not the whole body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'דבר' shows that liability applies only when part of a מצוה is hidden.

steps.title: Source that the כהן משיח follows the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the same partial-ruling rule applies to the כהן משיח. The גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same for the anointed priest. From where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'דבר' rule was said about the court. The גמרא wants to know why the כהן משיח also needs a partial ruling to be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise
The anointed כהן גדול

phrases.english: And likewise the anointed priest.
From where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the כהן משיח also needs a partial ruling.

steps.title: 'לאשמת העם' makes the priest like the community
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'לאשמת העם' shows that the כהן משיח is treated like the community, so the same rule applies to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written: 'to bring guilt on the people.' So the anointed priest is like the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that links the כהן משיח to the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects the priest's sin to 'the people'. So the rules for a community ruling also apply to him, including the need for a partial ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring guilt on the people
The community

phrases.english: As it is written: "to bring guilt on the people,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3

phrases.english: so the anointed priest is like the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כהן משיח is compared to the community, so the 'דבר' rule applies to him too.

steps.title: Source that the rule applies to עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the court and the priest are liable for עבודה זרה only through a partial ruling. The גמרא asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not for idol worship, etc. From where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה has its own separate set of קרבן laws, so one might think the general rules do not apply to it. The גמרא wants proof that the partial-ruling rule still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
Etc.; the rest of the משנה's line

phrases.english: And not with idol worship, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line is: not liable for עבודה זרה unless they rule to cancel part and keep part.

phrases.english: From where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for requiring a partial ruling for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A ברייתא starts: maybe a full uprooting counts for עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא. Since עבודה זרה was given its own section, one might think they are liable even for uprooting the whole מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: since idol worship was taken out to be dealt with by itself, one might think they are liable for uprooting the entire מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first raises a possible mistaken idea, which the next step rejects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה has a separate passage in the תורה, so one might think it has its own rules. Then even uprooting the whole prohibition would make them liable. The ברייתא states this idea so it can reject it next.

keyTerms.meaning: To be dealt with by itself
One might think (introduces a possible mistaken idea)
Uprooting the entire מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the ברייתא's conclusion. The word 'יכול' introduces an idea the ברייתא is about to reject.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
Since idol worship was taken out
to be dealt with by itself,
phrases.notes: עבודה זרה gets its own separate section about קרבנות in the תורה (במדבר 15).

phrases.english: one might think they are liable
for uprooting the entire מצוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן לְפִי שֶׁיָּצְאָה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לָדוּן בְּעַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 14 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא begins by raising the idea that a full uprooting might count for עבודה זרה; step 16 rejects it.

steps.title: The word 'from the eyes of' links עבודה זרה to the other מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its answer with a גזירה שוה. 'מֵעֵינֵי' appears both by עבודה זרה and by the regular communal sin-offering, so the same rules apply: the ruling must come from בית דין, and it must cancel only part of a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'from the eyes of' is written here (by עבודה זרה), and the same word is written there (by the other מצוות). Just as there it means a ruling by the court, here too it means a ruling by the court. And just as there it means only part of a מצוה and not the whole thing, here too it means only part of a מצוה and not the whole thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea from step 15 that the court would be liable for uprooting all of עבודה זרה. It proves this by matching a word that shows up in both sections of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 suggested that because עבודה זרה has its own section, its rules might be different. The shared word 'מֵעֵינֵי' ties the two sections together, so everything true about the other מצוות carries over. That means the ruling must come from the court, and it must uproot only part of the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from a word that appears in two places in the תורה
'From the eyes of', meaning hidden from the eyes of the leaders, the court
'There', meaning the other place in the תורה
The entire body, meaning the whole מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: Even for עבודה זרה, the court is liable only for a ruling that uproots part of a מצוה, never the whole thing. This is learned from the shared word 'מֵעֵינֵי'.

phrases.english: It is stated here, 'from the eyes of,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:24, the section about עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: and it is stated there, 'from the eyes of.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13, the regular communal sin-offering.

phrases.english: Just as there it is about the court,
so too here it is about the court.
And just as there it is 'a matter' and not the entire body,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן נָמֵי ״דָּבָר״ וְלֹא כׇּל הַגּוּף.
phrases.english: so too here it is 'a matter' and not the entire body.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן מֵעֵינֵי וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן מֵעֵינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 15 by rejecting its first suggestion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on 'מֵעֵינֵי' applies the partial-ruling rule and the court requirement to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: A new משנה: both a mistaken ruling and a mistaken action are needed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the court is liable only when a mistaken ruling (העלם דבר) leads to an action done by mistake (שגגת המעשה). The same is true for the כהן משיח and for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court is liable only for a hidden matter together with an unwitting action. The same is true of the anointed priest. And it is no different with עבודה זרה: they are liable only for a hidden matter together with an unwitting action.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out a second condition for bringing the special קרבן: a mistaken ruling, plus people actually acting on it by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the topic was what kind of ruling counts, which is a partial one. Now the משנה adds that a ruling alone is not enough, and neither is a mistaken action alone. Both must happen together, and this rule covers the court, the כהן משיח, and עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
A matter being hidden, meaning a mistaken ruling about the law
An action done by mistake
The anointed priest, the כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'וְלֹא בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה' do not mean עבודה זרה is excluded. They mean עבודה זרה is no different and follows the same rule.

phrases.english: MISHNAH

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין אֶלָּא עַל הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר
phrases.english: They are liable only for a hidden matter
phrases.notes: 'Hidden matter' means the court ruled wrongly because the real law was hidden from them.

phrases.english: together with an unwitting action,
and likewise the anointed priest,
and it is no different with idol worship:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין אֶלָּא עַל הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר
phrases.english: they are liable only for a hidden matter
together with an unwitting action.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין חַיָּיבִין אֶלָּא עַל הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר עִם שִׁגְגַת הַמַּעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court, the כהן משיח, and cases of עבודה זרה all need both a mistaken ruling and an action done by mistake because of it.

steps.title: Where do we learn that both conditions are needed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the court needs both a mistaken ruling and a mistaken action.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the פסוק behind the first rule of the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule without a source. The גמרא wants to know which words in the תורה show that a mistaken action alone is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the משנה
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for requiring both העלם דבר and שגגת המעשה.

steps.title: 'They shall err, and a matter was hidden' teaches both conditions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that 'יִשְׁגּוּ' alone might suggest liability for any mistaken action. The added words 'וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר' require a mistaken ruling as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: 'They shall err.' I might think they are liable for any action done by mistake. So the פסוק says, 'They shall err, and a matter was hidden.' They are liable only for a hidden matter together with an unwitting action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that reads the words of ויקרא 4:13 closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יִשְׁגּוּ' (erring) points to the mistaken action. The next words, 'וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר', add the mistaken ruling. Since both appear in the פסוק, both are required.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall err, meaning they act by mistake
I might have thought
The פסוק teaches us

phrases.english: As the rabbis taught: 'They shall err' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: I might think they would be liable
for an unwitting action alone?
So the verse says:
'They shall err, and a matter was hidden,'

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין אֶלָּא עַל הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר
phrases.english: they are liable only for a hidden matter
together with an unwitting action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'יִשְׁגּוּ וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר' require both a mistaken action and a mistaken ruling.

steps.title: Where do we learn the same for the כהן משיח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'and likewise the anointed priest' and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And likewise the anointed priest.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and asks how we know the כהן משיח also needs both conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'יִשְׁגּוּ וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר' was said about the community. The גמרא needs a reason to apply it to the כהן משיח as well.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise

phrases.english: 'And likewise the anointed priest.' From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the court's rule to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the כהן משיח also needs both העלם דבר and שגגת המעשה.

steps.title: The כהן משיח is treated like the community
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' shows that the כהן משיח is like the ציבור, so the community's rule applies to him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written, 'to bring guilt on the people.' This shows the anointed priest is like the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same פסוק it used in step 13. It links the כהן משיח to the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' connects the כהן משיח's sin to the people, so his laws follow theirs. Since the community needs both a mistaken ruling and a mistaken action, so does he. The גמרא really does repeat this source here, because this משנה is teaching a new rule.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring guilt on the people
Like the community

steps.whatToRemember: The court and the כהן משיח need both a mistaken ruling and an action done by mistake because of it. For the court this comes from 'יִשְׁגּוּ וְנֶעֱלַם דָּבָר', and for the כהן משיח from 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם'.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'to bring guilt on the people,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:3

phrases.english: so the anointed priest is like the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 with the same source used in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לְאַשְׁמַת הָעָם' makes the כהן משיח like the community, so he too needs both conditions.

steps.title: What is the source for the עבודה זרה rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about עבודה זרה and asks how we know that it also needs a mistaken ruling together with a mistaken action.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not with עבודה זרה, except for a mistaken ruling together with a mistaken action.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next piece of the משנה, about עבודה זרה, and asks for its source. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps proved the 'both ingredients' rule for regular sins. עבודה זרה has its own section in the תורה, so the גמרא needs a separate source showing the same rule applies there too.

keyTerms.meaning: Idol worship
A 'hidden matter': the court forgot the law and gave a mistaken ruling
An action done by mistake
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And not with idol worship
except for a hidden matter (a mistaken ruling)
together with a mistaken action.
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כהן משיח clause of the משנה to the עבודה זרה clause and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that liability for עבודה זרה also requires both a mistaken ruling and a mistaken action.

steps.title: A shared word links עבודה זרה to other sins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא uses the word 'מֵעֵינֵי', found in both sections, to show that עבודה זרה follows the same rule as other sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Since עבודה זרה was taken out to be discussed on its own, you might think they are liable for just a mistaken action. But 'מֵעֵינֵי' is said here, and 'מֵעֵינֵי' is said there. Just as there they are liable only for a mistaken ruling together with a mistaken action, so too here they are liable only for a mistaken ruling together with a mistaken action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. It links the עבודה זרה section to the regular communal sin-offering section through a shared word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because עבודה זרה has its own separate section, we might have thought a simple mistaken act is enough there. The shared word 'מֵעֵינֵי' (a גזירה שוה) shows that the same requirement applies to both: a mistaken ruling plus a mistaken action.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taken out to be discussed on its own (it has its own section)
'From the eyes of': the shared word that links the two sections
Here... there: the two places being compared
Learning one law from another because the same word appears in both

steps.whatToRemember: For עבודה זרה, just as for other sins, the court is liable only when a mistaken ruling leads to a mistaken action. We learn it from the shared word 'מֵעֵינֵי'.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
Since idol worship was taken out
to be discussed on its own,
phrases.notes: The Torah gives עבודה זרה its own separate section, in במדבר 15.

phrases.english: you might think they would be liable
for a mistaken action alone?
'From the eyes of' is said here
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:24

phrases.english: and 'from the eyes of' is said there.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:13

phrases.english: Just as there they are not liable
except for a mistaken ruling
together with a mistaken action,
so too here they are not liable
except for a mistaken ruling
together with a mistaken action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on 'מֵעֵינֵי' links עבודה זרה to the regular communal sin-offering, so both need a mistaken ruling plus a mistaken action.

steps.title: The משנה leaves out a priest who sins with עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the משנה never mentions a כהן משיח who sins with עבודה זרה, and asks whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה does not teach the case of a כהן משיח with עבודה זרה. Whose opinion is the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a gap: the משנה says nothing about a כהן משיח and עבודה זרה. It asks whose view explains this, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the 'mistaken ruling' rule for the כהן משיח and for עבודה זרה, but it never combined them. The silence suggests that for this case the priest may not follow the court's rule, so the גמרא looks for a תנא who holds that way.

keyTerms.meaning: The anointed כהן גדול
It is not taught (the משנה does not mention it)
Whose opinion is our משנה?

phrases.english: Whereas an anointed priest with idol worship
is not taught.
Whose opinion is our משנה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the עבודה זרה source, the גמרא notices what the משנה leaves out and asks whose view it reflects.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view explains why the משנה does not apply the 'mistaken ruling' rule to a כהן משיח who sins with עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה follows רבי, who holds that a כהן משיח who sins with עבודה זרה is treated like an ordinary Jew. A ברייתא shows the מחלוקת and the points both sides agree on. Steps 26–27 reject this proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי. As it was taught: a כהן משיח with עבודה זרה: רבי says he brings an offering for a mistaken action. The חכמים say he brings it only for a mistaken ruling. Both agree that he brings a female goat, and both agree that he does not bring an אשם תלוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי. It then quotes a ברייתא where רבי and the חכמים argue about this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says the כהן משיח with עבודה זרה is like any Jew: a mistaken action alone makes him bring an offering. That is why the משנה did not list him with the 'mistaken ruling' rule. The חכמים require a mistaken ruling, but both sides agree that his offering is a female goat and that he never brings an אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree
A female goat, brought as a sin-offering
A 'hanging' guilt-offering, brought when unsure whether one sinned

steps.whatToRemember: רבי holds that a כהן משיח who sins with עבודה זרה is treated like an ordinary Jew, so a mistaken action alone is enough. The חכמים say he needs a mistaken ruling. Everyone agrees he brings a female goat and no אשם תלוי. The claim that our משנה follows רבי is only a suggestion; steps 26–27 reject the proof for it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two opinions. רבי says 'mistaken action' (like a regular person). The חכמים say 'mistaken ruling' (like the court). The idea that the משנה matches רבי because it left this case out is only a first suggestion, and the גמרא rejects it in steps 26–27.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi.
As it was taught in a ברייתא:
An anointed priest with idol worship:
Rabbi says: for a mistaken action.
phrases.notes: He means a mistaken act alone is enough for the priest to bring an offering, just like any Jew.

phrases.english: And the Sages say: for a mistaken ruling.
And they agree that it is with a female goat,
and they agree that he does not bring a provisional guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers whose opinion the משנה follows and backs it with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The suggested answer is that the משנה follows רבי, who treats a כהן משיח with עבודה זרה like an ordinary Jew (liable for a mistaken action alone). That would explain why the משנה did not include him in the 'mistaken ruling' rule. Steps 26-27 reject this proof.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the מחלוקת between רבי and the חכמים, along with their two points of agreement.

steps.title: Is leaving out the כהן משיח really a proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from the משנה's silence. Another משנה also leaves out the כהן משיח, yet nobody concludes anything from that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do you really think so? In the משנה about a sin whose intentional version gets כרת and whose mistaken version brings a חטאת, is the כהן משיח mentioned there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last step's proof that our משנה follows רבי because it does not mention the כהן משיח. It points to another משנה that also does not mention him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof was based only on silence: the משנה did not list the כהן משיח. But the משנה on 8a, about the rule of כרת and חטאת, also does not list him, even though he clearly follows that rule. So silence alone proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And do you really think so?' A way of pushing back on an idea
Doing a sin on purpose
Being cut off, the heavenly punishment for some sins done on purpose
'Does it teach?' A way of asking whether the משנה actually says something

phrases.english: And how can you understand it this way?
In the case of 'on purpose it gets כרת, by mistake it brings a חטאת,'
phrases.notes: He means the משנה on 8a, which teaches this rule for the בית דין.

phrases.english: does it teach the case of the כהן משיח?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on step 25's claim that the משנה must follow רבי
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה's silence about the כהן משיח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Another משנה is also silent about the כהן משיח without meaning he is excluded, so silence is not a proof

steps.title: The תנא teaches one case and the other follows
steps.stepSummary: Sometimes the תנא teaches one case and expects us to know the other works the same way. That is true in the other משנה, and it is true here too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the תנא teaches this case, and the same rule applies to that one. Here too, he taught this case, and the same rule applies to that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the כהן משיח is missing. The תנא taught the rule for one case and relied on us to apply it to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה on 8a, the כהן משיח was left out of the second part only because his rule there is obvious from the first part. The same can be said about our משנה. So our משנה could also follow the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The same rule applies.' What is said about one case also holds for another
'Here too'

steps.whatToRemember: Just because a משנה leaves out a case does not prove the case has a different rule. The תנא may teach one case and expect us to fill in the other.

phrases.english: Rather, he teaches this case,
and the same is true for that case.
Here too, he taught this case,
and the same is true for that case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תָּנֵי הָא הוּא הַדִּין לְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge of step 26 by explaining why the case was left out
steps.terutzResolutionType: Teaching style: one case is taught and the other is understood from it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out the כהן משיח means the משנה must follow רבי
steps.terutzMaskana: Leaving him out is just the תנא's style, so the משנה can follow the רבנן

steps.title: What is רבי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבי's source for treating a כהן משיח who sins with עבודה זרה like an ordinary Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי gets his view. This sets up the next step, which brings the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי said that for עבודה זרה, a כהן משיח brings his offering like a regular person, for a mistaken act alone. The גמרא wants the source in the תורה for this unusual rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the reason?' A request for someone's source or logic

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי's view from step 25 and asks for its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind רבי's rule that a כהן משיח who sins with עבודה זרה is like an ordinary person

steps.title: רבי reads 'בְּחֶטְאָה בִשְׁגָגָה' as a simple mistaken act
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about עבודה זרה includes the כהן משיח and the נשיא. The words 'בְּחֶטְאָה בִשְׁגָגָה' tell רבי that this sin needs only a mistaken act.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the כהן shall atone for the soul that acted by mistake, when it sins by mistake.' 'The soul' is the כהן משיח. 'That acted by mistake' is the נשיא. 'When it sins by mistake': רבי holds this sin should be a plain mistaken act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי's source. He reads each part of the פסוק in במדבר 15 about עבודה זרה as including someone, and he reads the end as setting the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a כהן משיח brings a חטאת only when he made a mistaken ruling and then acted on it. Here the פסוק stresses 'by mistake'. רבי takes that to mean that for עבודה זרה, a plain mistaken act is enough, just like for any person.

keyTerms.meaning: The leader or king, who has his own rules for a חטאת
A mistake, a sin done without knowing
'Holds,' meaning he understands it this way

phrases.english: The פסוק says:
'And the כהן shall atone for the soul'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:28

phrases.english: 'that acted by mistake, when it sins by mistake.'
'The soul': this is the כהן משיח,
'that acted by mistake': this is the נשיא,
'when it sins by mistake':

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי סָבַר: חֵטְא זֶה בִּשְׁגָגָה יְהֵא.
phrases.english: רבי holds: this sin should be a simple mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 with the פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'בְּחֶטְאָה בִשְׁגָגָה' show that for עבודה זרה, the כהן משיח brings his offering for a plain mistaken act, like an ordinary person

steps.title: The רבנן read the same words to leave out the כהן משיח
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say 'בְּחֶטְאָה בִשְׁגָגָה' describes someone whose חטאת always comes for a plain mistake. That leaves out the כהן משיח, whose חטאת comes only with a mistaken ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן hold: the words mean someone whose חטאת is for a plain mistake. This leaves out the כהן משיח, whose חטאת is not for a plain mistake, but only with a mistaken ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the רבנן understand the same words. For them, these words leave the כהן משיח out of the ordinary person's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same words but read them differently. רבי says the words describe the sin: a plain mistake is enough. The רבנן say the words describe the person: only someone whose חטאת normally comes for a plain mistake. A כהן משיח always needs a mistaken ruling, so he keeps his own rule even for עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The majority of the Sages, who disagree with רבי here
'Leaves out.' Shows who is not included in a rule
A mistaken ruling, where the law itself was forgotten or misjudged

steps.whatToRemember: רבי reads 'בְּחֶטְאָה בִשְׁגָגָה' as 'this sin is a plain mistake,' so the כהן משיח is like anyone else. The רבנן read it as 'one whose חטאת is for a plain mistake,' so the כהן משיח is left out and still needs a mistaken ruling.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions come from the very same words. They argue only about whether the words describe the kind of sin or the kind of person.

phrases.english: And the רבנן hold:
it means one whose חטאת is for a plain mistake,
which leaves out the כהן משיח,
whose חטאת is not for a plain mistake,
but only when there was a mistaken ruling.
phrases.notes: He means a mistaken ruling followed by acting on it, as in step 21.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the רבנן's reading of the same words רבי used in step 29
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words limit the ordinary rule to people whose חטאת comes for a plain mistake, so the כהן משיח still needs a mistaken ruling

steps.title: Both sides agree he brings a female goat like an individual
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא picks up the next clause of the ברייתא: רבי and the רבנן agree that a כהן משיח's קרבן for עבודה זרה is a שעירה, like an ordinary person's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that his offering is a female goat, like an individual's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא, where רבי and the רבנן agree on one point. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי and the רבנן argued about what makes a כהן משיח liable for עבודה זרה: a mistaken act alone, or a mistaken ruling. Here they agree on what he brings once he is liable. For other sins a כהן משיח brings a פר, but for עבודה זרה he brings a שעירה, exactly like a regular יחיד.

keyTerms.meaning: they agree (both רבי and the רבנן)
a female goat brought as a חטאת
an ordinary individual (not a כהן משיח or נשיא)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two questions. The argument was about WHEN he is liable. The agreement here is about WHAT animal he brings.

phrases.english: And they agree that it is with a female goat, like an individual.
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי and the רבנן. "It" is the כהן משיח's קרבן for עבודה זרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the argument between רבי and the רבנן to the point they agree on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן משיח who brings a קרבן for עבודה זרה brings a שעירה, the same as an ordinary יחיד.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the agreement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a כהן משיח brings a שעירה for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule both sides just agreed on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כהן משיח brings a פר for his sin. So it is surprising that for עבודה זרה he brings the same animal as a regular person, and the גמרא wants to see where the תורה says so.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know it? (a request for a source)
the anointed כהן גדול

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the agreed rule in Step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that a כהן משיח brings a שעירה for עבודה זרה, like an individual.

steps.title: 'One soul' includes the individual, the נשיא, and the כהן משיח
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'וְאִם נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת', and that phrase covers the יחיד, the נשיא, and the כהן משיח alike, so all of them bring a שעירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'And if one soul.' An individual, a נשיא, and a כהן משיח are all included in 'one soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. 'נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת' means any single person, so it includes the נשיא and the כהן משיח together with a regular person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a single person's sin of עבודה זרה commands a שעירה. Since 'one soul' is a general term, it does not leave out anyone with a special rank. So for this sin the כהן משיח and the נשיא bring the same animal as everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: a פסוק
'one soul': any single person
the leader or king
included in

steps.whatToRemember: For עבודה זרה, a כהן משיח does not bring his usual פר. Because 'נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת' includes him, he brings a שעירה like any יחיד. On this point both רבי and the רבנן agree.

phrases.english: As the verse says: "And if one soul"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:27

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד יָחִיד וְאֶחָד נָשִׂיא וְאֶחָד מָשִׁיחַ
phrases.english: Whether an individual, or a נשיא, or an anointed כהן
They are all included in "one soul."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The general phrase 'נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת' in the פסוק commanding a שעירה includes the יחיד, the נשיא, and the כהן משיח.
